인지과학 연구의 중요한 함의 중 하나는. <break time="0.8s" /> 흔한 믿음 가정 중 다수가. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람이 어떻게 생각하고 결정을 내리는지에 관한. <break time="0.8s" /> 틀렸다는 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 미래 전망 나 과거 회고 에 대해 생각하는 것은. <break time="0.8s" /> 같은 정신 과정을 사용한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 현재에 대해 생각하는 것과. <break time="0.8s" /> 기억은 머릿속에서 다시 만들어진다. <break time="0.8s" /> 과거의 사건이 떠올려질 때. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 글자 그대로 부호화된 기록이 아니다. <break time="0.8s" /> 일어난 일의 사진과 같은 기록 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 따라서, 가능하다. <break time="0.8s" /> 거짓 기억을 갖는 것이. <break time="0.8s" /> 또 다른 함의는 그것이 도전한다는 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 계몽주의적 관점에. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 인간은 합리적이고 논리적이라는 관점에 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 믿음이 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 합리적 사고가 발전으로 이어져 왔다는. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 기술과 과학, 의학과 수학 분야의 발전 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러나 감정적이라는 것이 의미하지는 않는다. <break time="0.8s" /> 비합리적이라는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 실제로, 감정은 무의식적이지만 합리적이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 인간 생존의 바탕이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 쾌락으로 행동을 부추기거나 공포로 행동을 말림으로써. <break time="0.8s" /> 많은 결정은 내려진다. <break time="0.8s" /> 감정적 반응과 뒤따르는 느낌에 근거해. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러나 사후에 논리적인 것으로 합리화된다. <break time="0.8s" /> 따라서, 인지과학에 대한 지식은 필수적이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람들과 그들의 행동을 이해하는 데.

One of the important implications of the study of cognitive science is that many of common beliefs assumptions about how one thinks and makes decisions are incorrect. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking about the future prospection or past retrospection uses the same mental processes as thinking about the present. <break time="0.8s" /> Memories are mentally recreated when a past event is recalled and not a verbatim encoded record like a picture of what happened. <break time="0.8s" /> Therefore, it is possible to have false memories. <break time="0.8s" /> Another implication is that it challenges the enlightenment view that humans are rational and logical. <break time="0.8s" /> There is a belief that rational thought has led to advances in technology and science, medicine and mathematics. <break time="0.8s" /> But being emotional does not mean being irrational. <break time="0.8s" /> Indeed, emotions are unconscious but rational and are the basis for human survival by encouraging pleasure or discouraging fear action. <break time="0.8s" /> Many decisions are made based on emotional reactions and subsequent feelings but are rationalised as logical after the fact. <break time="0.8s" /> Therefore, knowledge of cognitive science is essential to understand people and their actions.

대중문화에서 속어의 역할은. <break time="0.8s" /> 근본적으로 바뀌었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 인터넷 때문에. <break time="0.8s" /> 표준 영어의 등장 이래로. <break time="0.8s" /> 언어의 규칙 제정자들이 주도권을 쥐어 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그들의 규범적 기준이. <break time="0.8s" /> 올바른 영어라는 것에 관한. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리의 소통 통로를 지배해 왔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 만약 당신의 목소리가 대중에게 들리기를 원했다면. <break time="0.8s" /> 당신은 그들의 제약 안에서 일해야 했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 엄격한 기대에 따르면서. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 인쇄 매체든 방송 매체든 그 매체가 가진 기대 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 소셜 미디어가 완전히 부숴 버렸다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 장벽을. <break time="0.8s" /> 경기장은 이제 평평하다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 대중의 접근은 민주화되었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 어느 누구든 그리고 모든 사람이 공인이 될 수 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 새로운 소통 플랫폼에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 이는 아무도 남아 있지 않다는 뜻이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 옛 규칙을 강제할 사람이 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> TV 진행자와 기자들은. <break time="0.8s" /> 속어를 쓸 수 없었을지 모른다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 콘텐츠 창작자들은 쓸 수 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리는 function과 side eye 같은 단어를 일상적으로 쓴다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 우리의 영향력은 이 용어들을 정당화할 뿐 아니라. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것들에게 큰 무대를 준다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 전에 그럴 수 있었던 것보다 더 빨리 퍼지게 한다.

The role of slang in popular culture has fundamentally changed because of the internet. <break time="0.8s" /> Since the emergence of Standard English, the rule makers of language have been in charge, and their prescriptive norms about a correct version of the English language have dominated our channels of communication. <break time="0.8s" /> If you wanted your voice to be heard by the public, you had to work within their constraints, conforming to the stringent expectations of either print or broadcast media. <break time="0.8s" /> Social media completely shattered that barrier. <break time="0.8s" /> The playing field is now level, and public access is democratized. <break time="0.8s" /> Anybody and everybody can become a public figure on the new communicative platforms, meaning that nobodys left to enforce the old rules. <break time="0.8s" /> TV presenters and journalists might not have been able to use slang, but content creators can. <break time="0.8s" /> We regularly use words like function and side eye, and our influence both legitimizes these terms and gives them a large platform to spread quicker than they could have before.

Research shows how we can tell, just from their talk. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether people know one another. <break time="0.8s" /> Because of the way they treat conversational hypertext. <break time="0.8s" /> As needing no further explanation. <break time="0.8s" /> Planalp and Garvin Doxas reported a number of studies. <break time="0.8s" /> Where they played tapes of talk to an audience. <break time="0.8s" /> And asked the listeners to say. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether the people on the tape were friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Listeners were very skilled at making this identification. <break time="0.8s" /> And could easily tell. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether two conversational partners were acquainted. <break time="0.8s" /> Or merely strangers. <break time="0.8s" /> What made the difference was whether or not the talkers took information for granted. <break time="0.8s" /> Or whether they explained the terms used. <break time="0.8s" /> Said without explanation. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim was worried about his foot again. <break time="0.8s" /> Identified the two conversers as friends. <break time="0.8s" /> On the other hand, the following showed them to be unacquainted. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim, that is my friend from high school. <break time="0.8s" /> Was worried about his foot again. <break time="0.8s" /> He has gout and has to be careful about setting it off. <break time="0.8s" /> It is a problem that keeps coming back. <break time="0.8s" /> It worries him a lot. <break time="0.8s" /> So he usually calls me when it flares up. <break time="0.8s" /> And I have to deal with it.

연구는 우리가 단지 그들의 대화만으로 어떻게 알 수 있는지 보여 준다. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람들이 서로 아는 사이인지를. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들이 대화의 하이퍼텍스트를 다루는 방식 때문에. <break time="0.8s" /> 더 이상의 설명이 필요 없는 것으로. <break time="0.8s" /> Planalp과 Garvin Doxas는 여러 연구를 보고했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 연구에서 그들은 청중에게 대화 녹음테이프를 들려주었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 청자들에게 말해 달라고 요청했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 테이프 속 사람들이 친구인지를. <break time="0.8s" /> 청자들은 이런 판별을 하는 데 매우 능숙했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 쉽게 알 수 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 두 대화 상대가 아는 사이인지. <break time="0.8s" /> 아니면 단지 낯선 사람들인지. <break time="0.8s" /> 차이를 만든 것은 다음이었다 화자들이 정보를 당연한 것으로 여기는지 아닌지. <break time="0.8s" /> 아니면 그들이 쓰인 용어들을 설명하는지. <break time="0.8s" /> 설명 없이 말해진. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim이 또 발 때문에 걱정했어는. <break time="0.8s" /> 두 대화자를 친구로 식별해 주었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 반면에, 다음 말은 그들이 모르는 사이임을 보여 주었다. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim이, 걔는 내 고등학교 친구인데. <break time="0.8s" /> 또 발 때문에 걱정했어. <break time="0.8s" /> 걔는 통풍이 있어서 그게 도지지 않게 조심해야 하거든. <break time="0.8s" /> 그건 계속 재발하는 문제야. <break time="0.8s" /> 그게 걔를 많이 괴롭혀서. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래서 그게 갑자기 심해지면 걔가 보통 나한테 전화하고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 내가 그걸 처리해야 해.

Research shows how we can tell, just from their talk, whether people know one another because of the way they treat conversational hypertext as needing no further explanation. <break time="0.8s" /> Planalp and Garvin Doxas reported a number of studies where they played tapes of talk to an audience and asked the listeners to say whether the people on the tape were friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Listeners were very skilled at making this identification and could easily tell whether two conversational partners were acquainted or merely strangers. <break time="0.8s" /> What made the difference was whether or not the talkers took information for granted or whether they explained the terms used. <break time="0.8s" /> Said without explanation, Jim was worried about his foot again identified the two conversers as friends. <break time="0.8s" /> On the other hand, the following showed them to be unacquainted, Jim, that is my friend from high school, was worried about his foot again, He has gout and has to be careful about setting it off, it is a problem that keeps coming back, It worries him a lot, so he usually calls me when it flares up, and I have to deal with it.

If you are starting a new project. <break time="0.8s" /> You might set aside time. <break time="0.8s" /> To conduct a premortem. <break time="0.8s" /> Premortems involve imagining a future time. <break time="0.8s" /> At which you have come to the end of the project. <break time="0.8s" /> And realized that it was a complete disaster. <break time="0.8s" /> You then try to explain. <break time="0.8s" /> What went wrong and why. <break time="0.8s" /> Premortems can be a great way. <break time="0.8s" /> To make the abstract idea of the project concrete. <break time="0.8s" /> More than this, they are a great remedy. <break time="0.8s" /> For the overconfidence we often experience. <break time="0.8s" /> At the beginning of a project. <break time="0.8s" /> Assessments of premortems bear this out. <break time="0.8s" /> For example, in an exercise involving disaster recovery planning. <break time="0.8s" /> Those who conducted a premortem. <break time="0.8s" /> Were much less confident in their plan at the end. <break time="0.8s" /> Than those who did not. <break time="0.8s" /> While underconfidence is not generally a good thing. <break time="0.8s" /> The right level of confidence helps us adjust. <break time="0.8s" /> Our approach to a task effectively. <break time="0.8s" /> Revising down confidence estimates likely reflects the fact. <break time="0.8s" /> That the participants simply had a better sense. <break time="0.8s" /> Of what it would take to succeed.

만약 당신이 새 프로젝트를 시작하고 있다면. <break time="0.8s" /> 당신은 시간을 따로 떼어 둘 수도 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 프리모텀을 실시할. <break time="0.8s" /> 프리모텀은 미래의 시점을 상상하는 것을 포함한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 시점에 당신은 프로젝트의 끝에 다다랐다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그것이 완전한 재앙이었음을 깨달았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그런 다음 당신은 설명하려고 노력한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 무엇이 잘못되었고 왜 그랬는지. <break time="0.8s" /> 프리모텀은 훌륭한 방법이 될 수 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 프로젝트라는 추상적인 아이디어를 구체적으로 만드는. <break time="0.8s" /> 이보다 더 나아가, 그것들은 훌륭한 치료제이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리가 흔히 경험하는 과신에 대한. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 프로젝트 초기에 경험하는 과신 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 프리모텀에 대한 평가 결과들이 이를 입증한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 예를 들어, 재난 복구 계획을 수반하는 한 연습에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 프리모텀을 실시한 사람들은. <break time="0.8s" /> 마지막에 자신들의 계획에 훨씬 덜 자신했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그렇게 하지 않은 사람들보다. <break time="0.8s" /> 자신감 부족이 일반적으로 좋은 것은 아니지만. <break time="0.8s" /> 적절한 수준의 자신감은 우리가 조정하도록 돕는다. <break time="0.8s" /> 과제에 대한 우리의 접근법을 효과적으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 자신감 추정치를 하향 조정한 것은 아마 다음 사실을 반영한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 참가자들이 그저 더 나은 감각을 갖게 되었다는. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 성공하는 데 무엇이 필요할지에 대한 감각 말이다.

If you are starting a new project, you might set aside time to conduct a premortem. <break time="0.8s" /> Premortems involve imagining a future time at which you have come to the end of the project and realized that it was a complete disaster. <break time="0.8s" /> You then try to explain what went wrong and why. <break time="0.8s" /> Premortems can be a great way to make the abstract idea of the project concrete. <break time="0.8s" /> More than this, they are a great remedy for the overconfidence we often experience at the beginning of a project. <break time="0.8s" /> Assessments of premortems bear this out. <break time="0.8s" /> For example, in an exercise involving disaster recovery planning, those who conducted a premortem were much less confident in their plan at the end than those who did not. <break time="0.8s" /> While underconfidence is not generally a good thing, the right level of confidence helps us adjust our approach to a task effectively. <break time="0.8s" /> Revising down confidence estimates likely reflects the fact that the participants simply had a better sense of what it would take to succeed.
